subject: Mythology
title: The Pharaoh as a Living God
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Pharaoh as a Living God.

hook.text: The pharaoh was not just a king. Egyptians believed he was a god walking among mortals in human form.

buildup.text: Each pharaoh was considered the living incarnation of Horus and the son of Ra, the supreme sun god.

discovery.text: He was responsible for maintaining Ma'at. If the pharaoh failed, the gods would send famine and chaos.

twist.text: After death, the pharaoh merged with Osiris and ruled in the afterlife, replaced by the next living Horus.

climax.text: This divine kingship lasted over three thousand years, making it the longest-running political system in history.

punchline.text: One myth kept the same government running for three millennia.

quiz.question: Which god was the pharaoh believed to be the living incarnation of?
options: Osiris, the king of the dead
Anubis, the guardian of the dead
